recipe_version.title: Chinese Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry over Rice
recipe_version.description: The Chinese home-cooking classic: soft, fluffy scrambled eggs folded into juicy tomatoes cooked down with garlic, ginger, a little sugar, soy sauce, and scallions into a glossy sweet-savory sauce, spooned over jasmine rice.

steps.title: Start the rice and prep
steps.body: Combine the rinsed rice and 2 1/4 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes, then rest covered off the heat. While it comes to a boil, cut the tomatoes into wedges, mince the garlic and ginger, and slice the scallions. Beat the eggs with 1/2 tsp salt. Stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, sugar, and 1/4 cup water in a small bowl.

steps.title: Soft-scramble the eggs
steps.body: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high until shimmering. Pour in the eggs, let them puff for 10 seconds, then push them gently into large soft curds, about 1 minute, until just set but still glossy. Slide them into a bowl. The rice is cooking covered during this and the next steps (overlap stated).

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps.body: Return the wok to high with 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the garlic, ginger, and scallion whites for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook, pressing a few wedges with the spatula, until they collapse and release their juice, 5 to 6 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken and fold
steps.body: Stir the slurry (the cornstarch, soy sauce, and sugar in 1/4 cup water) and pour it in; simmer 1 minute until glossy and thick. Return the eggs and fold over medium heat for 30 seconds, keeping the curds large.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Fluff the rice, spoon the tomato and egg over it, and scatter the scallion greens.
